What happens while this is on
  • Every video that turns up in that folder — or in any folder inside it — is converted on its own, with the options set above.
  • A file is only picked up once it has stopped growing for 30 seconds, so a download that is still running is left alone.
  • What is already in the folder when you switch on is taken along. Finished results and their sources are skipped, and so is the originals folder.
  • Watching only lasts while this window is open — closing it ends the standing order.
  • The results are written next to their sources, and your originals are moved wherever your INI says. The watched folder will look different afterwards.

What this does

Takes each file in the queue apart for DaVinci Resolve: a silent picture file plus every audio track and every subtitle as its own file, written next to the source.

The details
  • Nothing is re-encoded — the picture and the audio are copied as they are.
  • Your source file stays where it is and is not touched.
  • Files with more than one track open a chooser, so you decide what gets pulled out.
  • Audio with more than two channels can additionally be written as a stereo mix — it is in the chooser as its own line.
There are no options here: this mode copies, it does not encode. What the Convert area is set to makes no difference.

What this does

Takes each file in the queue apart into its raw parts — a silent picture, every audio track and every subtitle as its own file, written next to the source. Nothing is re-encoded and nothing is cleaned up, so Join can put it back together unchanged.

The details
  • Every track is copied exactly as it is: audio keeps its own format (.ac3, .dts, .eac3, .m4a, .flac …), subtitles stay untouched.
  • The silent picture keeps the source container — an MP4 stays an MP4, everything else becomes MKV.
  • Your source file stays where it is and is not touched.
  • Files with more than one track open a chooser, so you decide what gets pulled out.
  • No stereo mix here: a downmix would be a re-encode, and this mode never re-encodes.
Not sure which one? DaVinci makes the parts ready for Resolve — audio as AAC, subtitles cleaned. Split keeps everything bit for bit as it was.

Files to join

Drop the video file plus its audio and subtitle files here They are sorted by extension. Dropping a folder adds the files inside it.

What this does

Builds one new MKV out of separate parts: a video file plus the audio and subtitle files you drop next to it. Every stream is copied exactly as it is — nothing is re-encoded.

The details
  • The audio files you add replace the sound of the video file. Add subtitles only, and the video keeps its own sound.
  • Subtitles already inside the video file are never carried over — add them as files.
  • Your files stay where they are; the result is always a new file next to the video file.
  • One job per run: exactly one video file, plus at least one audio or subtitle file.
  • A .sub only works together with its .idx of the same name — drop both.
  • The converter names the result itself: it tidies the base name (spaces become dots) and falls back to .joined2.mkv if that name is already taken.
The video can be .mkv .mp4 .m4v .mov — other formats cannot be used as a base here.
